did.unittitle: Collection of material about World War II
did.abstract: The Collection of material about World War II was compiled by UCLA Library Special Collections during the war and in the years following it. It includes publications by various governments and private groups covering myriad aspects of the war. It includes material from North and South America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.
did.physloc: Stored off-site. All requests to access special collections material must be made in advance using the request button located on this page.
did.langmaterial: In roughly descending order of frequency, materials are in English, Italian, French, Danish, Dutch, Japanese, German, Slovenian, Chinese, Norwegian, Spanish, Russian, and Polish.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Collections are processed to a variety of levels depending on the work necessary to make them usable, their perceived user interest and research value, availability of staff and resources, and competing priorities. Library Special Collections provides a standard level of preservation and access for all collections and, when time and resources permit, conducts more intensive processing. These materials have been arranged and described according to national and local standards and best practices.

We are committed to providing ethical, inclusive, and anti-racist description of the materials we steward, and to remediating existing description of our materials that contains language that may be offensive or cause harm. We invite you to submit feedback about how our collections are described, and how they could be described more accurately, by filling out the form located on our website: Report Problematic Content and Description in UCLA's Library Collections and Archives.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection includes publications by various governments and private groups covering myriad aspects of the war. It includes material from North and South America, Europe, Asia, and Africa. There are books, pamphlets, and periodicals of both an informational and propagandistic nature. There is extremely thorough documentation of the Allied Military Government in northeast Italy. There are a large number of scripts and other source material for theatrical shows at U.S. military facilities. There are also posters, maps, flags, and phonograph records. There is also postwar material, with a small amount of documentation of the military occupation of Germany and Japan, and a very large amount about Italy.
